title: Add a token-bucket rate limiter to a Go HTTP server
description: A Go HTTP server needs a token-bucket rate limiter. Add NewRateLimiter, Allow, and refill logic. Tests verify burst allowance, blocking after burst, and token refill.

task_spec.prompt:
Implement the RateLimiter in ratelimiter.go:

1. NewRateLimiter(capacity, ratePerSec): Initialize tokens=capacity, cap=capacity, rate=ratePerSec, lastTime=time.Now(). Return a pointer.
2. Allow():
   a. Lock the mutex.
   b. Compute elapsed = time.Since(rl.lastTime).Seconds()
   c. Add rl.rate * elapsed tokens, capped at rl.cap: rl.tokens = min(rl.cap, rl.tokens + rl.rate*elapsed)
   d. Update rl.lastTime = time.Now()
   e. If rl.tokens >= 1.0: subtract 1 token, unlock, return true
   f. Otherwise: unlock, return false

Note: min() for float64 is available as math.Min in Go 1.21, or write inline.

Run `go test ./...` to verify all 3 tests pass.
success_criteria: Burst of capacity tokens allowed before denial
Tokens refill over time at ratePerSec
followup_prompts: Good. Now add input validation and error handling to the feature you just implemented. What should happen with invalid, missing, or malformed inputs? Update the implementation and tests to cover those cases.
Run `go test ./...` to verify everything including your new error handling. Fix any failures and confirm the feature is complete.
